stories.title: Prediction of IgE-mediated allergic reactions to beta-lactam antibiotics using machine learning models
stories.description: IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reactions to beta-lactam antibiotics represent one of the most prevalent and potentially life-threatening forms of drug allergy, often involving cutaneous, respiratory, gastrointestinal, and cardiovascular manifestations, including hypotension and hemodynamic instability. Conventional diagnostic approaches such as clinical history assessment and in vivo and in vitro testing are limited by suboptimal sensitivity and specificity as well as restricted availability for many patients. Given these limitations, intelligent data-driven models show promise as complementary tools for supporting more rapid and accurate assessments of allergic risk. This study aimed to develop, train, and evaluate machine-learning models for predicting IgE-mediated allergic reactions to beta-lactam antibiotics and to design a clinical decision-support tool intended to assist physicians in this field. Clinical data were collected from patients referred to an allergy clinic in Iran and subsequently curated for analysis. A total of 322 patient records were evaluated using nine independent variables: age, gender, culprit drug group, time since last reaction, reaction repetition, reaction with another drug from the same class, time-to-onset of drug reactions, reaction severity, and history of other allergies. Multiple machine-learning algorithms were implemented to predict the final clinical diagnosis as the dependent outcome variable, which was established according to EAACI-based clinical assessment. Within the limitations of the balanced single-centre dataset, Random Forest achieved the highest composite mean score in internal cross-validation (0.912), with accuracy of 0.90, sensitivity of 0.90, specificity of 0.89, F-score of 0.90, and AUC of 0.97. In same-centre temporal validation, the Random Forest model was applied to the independent 80-patient dataset without retraining or retuning and achieved accuracy of 0.96, sensitivity of 0.95, specificity of 0.98, F-score of 0.96, AUC of 0.99, and a composite mean score of 0.97. These findings suggest that machine-learning models, particularly Random Forest, may serve as adjunctive tools for structured risk stratification of suspected IgE-mediated beta-lactam hypersensitivity in an allergy-clinic setting. However, this single-centre, balanced, retrospective study should be considered preliminary, and the developed software should be regarded as a research decision-support prototype rather than a tool ready for routine clinical implementation. Further prospective, multicentre validation and direct comparison with established clinical risk-stratification approaches are required before clinical deployment.

stories.title: Integrating metabolomics and proteomics uncovers core carbon metabolic dysregulation in Wilms’ tumor in children
stories.description: The unclear etiology, insufficient molecular classification strategies, and lack of validated therapeutic targets pose a critical barrier to precision treatment for Wilms’ tumor (WT) in children. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate metabolic dysregulations in WT by integrating metabolomics and proteomics. Metabolomic analysis of plasma samples from 36 WT patients and 36 healthy controls revealed 14 differentially abundant metabolites, including 5 upregulated and 9 downregulated. Proteomic analysis of 7 WT tissues and matched adjacent noncancerous tissues identified 3,378 significantly differentially expressed proteins, of which 1,783 were upregulated and 1,595 were downregulated. Integrated multi-omics analysis further identified three aberrant pathways associated with core carbon metabolism dysregulation: the citric acid cycle, ascorbate and aldarate metabolism, and propanoate metabolism. Collectively, these preliminary findings suggest that dysregulated carbon metabolism is associated with WT pathogenesis.
